_golden.type: one case for each presence form: the visible range (viewport in cells), the cell caret, a range as one unit, and claims on ranges; with their wire frames and roster events. r1: an agent's cells after each kind of verb (AG1-AG4), sheet states (HS1), width and height units (UN1)
notes: r1: the sample now has two hidden sheets (Lists, sheetId 3, hidden; Setup, sheetId 4, very hidden), so the sheet the turn adds is @sheet:5
state: keyed-state-rev20.json unless a case says otherwise. Row addresses name keys, not row numbers
MARKS: 'EXISTS' = on kit main 44c3c9ff; 'NEW' = asked by this addendum, not built

the frame type 'cells', the roster kind 'cells', the feature 'cells', the claim frame's 'cells' field and the roster kind 'claim_started_cells' are NEW names, proposed here; the kit picks the final spelling at its WIRE bump

a corner is {row, row_off, col, col_off}: the last keyed row (column) at or before the cell, then an offset. The kit refuses a corner that isn't in this form (MPC-E114), so two clients never spell one cell two ways
_a1 fields are annotations, not on the wire

cases.form: visible range (K2 Design ask 1)
cases.mark: EXISTS on the wire (viewport); NEW only as a declared meaning (the schema's grid slot says viewport is in cells)
cases.means: Ada sees columns 1-8 (A-H) and rows 1-30 of Budget

cases.form: visible range, scrolled part-way into a row
cases.means: visible rows are floor(y) to ceil(y + h) - 1, so rows 12-42, row 12 half shown; columns the same way

cases.form: visible range across an insert above it
cases.means: no event. A viewport is where a person's screen is, in row and column numbers, as a spreadsheet keeps the scroll place; the content under it moved down one row

cases.form: visible range when switching sheets
cases.means: the kit already orders focus first in a flush (WIRE 'Selection, pointer and viewport in the roster'); the viewport is read on the new focus sheet. Her cells value on Budget is dropped with the focus move (NEW rule)

cases.form: visible range refused

rows.from: a watcher past the participant cap

cases.form: cell caret (no range)
cases.also: setting cells sets the connection's focus to its container, as a text range does (NEW rule, by analogy with WIRE 'range')

cases.form: a range as ONE unit (K2 Design ask 2)
cases.compare_today: the existing 'select' names whole elements of one list root: here 4 row keys, and no way to say columns A-B or a blank cell

cases.form: a 10,000-cell range, mostly blank, still one unit
cases.means: row 1000 is 995 rows past the last keyed row (row 5); column J is 8 past the last keyed column (B). 10,000 cells, about 300 bytes on the wire

cases.form: several ranges (Ctrl-click)
a whole column and a whole row
cases.means: no special form: a whole column runs to the sheet's last row (1,048,576), a whole row to its last column (16,384). The view shows them as a column or row band

cases.form: a caret on a blank cell
cases._a1: A2 (row 2 is blank: one past keyed row 1)

cases.form: a range grows with an insert inside it
cases.mark: NEW (follows from keyed corners; the kit does nothing)
cases.means: rev 23 inserts @sheet:1/row:r19 between r8 and r9, both inside. No roster event: the corners did not change

cases.form: a corner's row is deleted
cases.change: an agent's rows delete removes row 15 (@sheet:1/row:r14, a list delete)
cases.means: the range is dropped, never moved or shrunk, as the kit drops a text range (WIRE 'range'). The active cell stays: its row is live. Sam's client sends a new value when he next moves

cases.form: an insert inside a blank stretch breaks a corner's form
cases.change: a row inserted at 16: a new keyed row now stands one past r14
cases.result: the corner {r14, 1} would now name the new row, which is not the cell the person chose (that blank row is now 17). The kit drops the range and sends the roster event, as CS8
cases.means: the kit checks each corner's form after every change that touches the rows or columns of a sheet with a cells value on it; a corner whose offset now reaches a keyed row is dropped

cases.form: focus moves to another sheet
cases.means: a PERSON's cells value is dropped (roster event cells: null in the same flush as the focus). See VR4 and presence-and-claims.json P3 (Ada). An agent's cells after a verb follow AG1-AG4 instead (r1)

cases.form: an agent's cells after a verb that writes cells (r1 ruling 1)
cases.rule: the frame's derived 'written' (the pack's rectangles, by corners at the frame's rev) becomes the agent's cells: ranges = written, active = the first range's start
cases.example: turn-frames.json rev 21: written D5:D7, then cells {active D5, ranges [D5:D7]} in the same flush

cases.form: after an insert (r1 ruling 2)
cases.rule: the inserted rows or columns, as whole-band ranges (a row band runs to column 16,384; a column band to row 1,048,576); active = the band's start
cases.example: rev 23: rows insert at 10, cells {active A10, ranges [A10:XFD10]}, which is also its 'written'

cases.form: after a delete (r1 ruling 2)
cases.rule: a caret on the first cell after the deleted band: for rows, column A of the first row after it; for columns, row 1 of the first column after it. No ranges. The frame has no 'written'; its 'bands' names the deleted band by its numbers before the change (ruling 4)
cases.example: rev 28: blank row 17 deleted, cells {active A17 = {row: @sheet:1/row:r15, row_off: 0, col: @sheet:1/col:c1, col_off: 0}, ranges []}; bands [{axis rows, op delete, from 17, to 17, numbers before}]

cases.form: after a sheet add or rename (r1 ruling 2)
cases.rule: focus moves to that sheet. The agent's cells are kept if they are on that sheet, else they become a caret at A1 of it

examples._a1: A1 of an empty sheet: no keyed row or column yet

cases.form: sheet states in the index (r1 ruling 6)
cases.means: hidden stays a bool for every view; state tells a view which hidden sheets the file hides from its own menus ('hidden by the file', Q-X14). From the sheet's state field: visible, hidden, veryHidden

cases.form: widths and heights (r1 ruling 8)
cases.mark: NEW (names only; the values EXIST in the store)

column_width.unit: characters of the default font's maximum digit width, as stored in the file

cases.means: the grid slot names both units. Pixels are K2's: points × 96 / 72 for heights; for widths, the default font's maximum digit width in pixels, which needs that font's metrics (HYPOTHESIS: the pack can derive the default font's name and size from the carrier's styles part, for K2 to measure)

cases.form: cells refused

rows.by: the client, unsent, and the host

rows.why: a corner's row is not live, or is on another sheet than 'container'
a corner not in its form: {row: @sheet:1/row:r1, row_off: 2} names row 3, which is keyed (@sheet:1/row:r2)
a position past the sheet's last row or column (1,048,576 by 16,384)
'active' outside every range when ranges are given

cases.rights: read, as select, pointer, viewport and focus

cases.form: a claim on a range, one unit
cases._a1: C4:D15 at the start; C4:D16 at the release
notes: claim_ended is the kit's existing event. For an element claim its 'lines' are list positions, for display only. For a cells claim this addendum proposes the range's first and last row NUMBERS on its sheet at that version (NEW meaning, computed through the grid slot's numbering): rows 4 and 16 at version 25, after the insert at rev 23. A list position would mean little here: the rows list is workbook-wide
an agent's cells claim moves its focus and replaces its cells value (NEW rule); its row selection is left alone

cases.form: what a cells claim holds off (agents only, under the host's ClaimPolicy::Respect)
cases.claim: claim-31, C4:D15 on Budget, by agent:atlas

rows.why: no claimed cell changes; the range grows (Q-X6v asks whether to refuse instead)
row fields (@hidden, @ht) are not cells; not covered in v1 (Q-X6v)
a claim never refuses a person (EXISTS rule); people write live only from slice X6
its own claim; held, so it does not end on the edit

cases.form: a claim on whole rows (EXISTS today)
cases.means: element claims on the rows root work today, up to 256 keyed rows. They can't name a blank row, columns, or a range of more than 256 rows. Cells claims (CC1) are for those
